gpu.explain: The graphics card. It does the heavy math for training and chat much faster than the main processor.

vram.explain: The memory on the GPU. A model and its training must fit in it, so it decides which models this machine can train.

ram.explain: The computer's main memory. Parts of a model can move here when the GPU is full. That works, but more slowly.

cpu.explain: The computer's main processor. It can run small models, slowly.

parameters.explain: The numbers a model learned during training. More parameters usually mean a more capable model that needs more memory.

context.explain: How much text the model can keep in view at once, counted in tokens. A longer context fits longer documents and chats.

thinking.explain: Some models write out their reasoning before the reply. That reasoning can be read and edited.

qlora.explain: A way to train a large model on a small GPU. Only a small part is trained, on top of a compressed copy of the model.

moe.explain: Mixture of experts. The model holds many specialist parts and uses only a few for each token, so it runs faster than its size suggests.

token.explain: A small piece of text, such as a short word or part of a word. Models split all text into tokens and count limits in them.

temperature.explain: How varied the model's word choices are. A low value gives steady, predictable replies. A high value gives more varied ones.

top_p.explain: Limits the next word to the most likely choices. At 0.9 the model picks only among the most likely words that together cover 90% of the probability. A lower value gives safer replies.

system_prompt.explain: The instructions every conversation starts with, before anyone types. They set the model's role, tone and rules.

version.explain: One saved state of the model. The first is the base model as downloaded. Each training run adds another, stored as a small change on top of the base.

lora.explain: A way to customize a model by training a small add-on on top of it. A version then needs little disk space and switches quickly.

delta.explain: Only what training changed in the model's parameters, stored on its own. The base model isn't copied into the version.

adapter.explain: The small file that holds a version's change. It is applied on top of the base model when the version runs.

engine.explain: A server that loads a model and answers messages. Mesbah has its own engine and can connect to others.

quantization.explain: Storing the model's numbers with fewer bits, so it takes less memory. Also called quantization. 4-bit needs about a quarter of the memory of 16-bit, with a small loss of quality.

api_key.explain: A secret code that lets a tool use Mesbah. It can do whatever the role of its owner allows.

openai_api.explain: The request format many tools and libraries already use. A tool made for it works with Mesbah once you change its address and key.

gguf.explain: A single-file model format that Ollama and llama.cpp load. A version must be exported to it before Ollama can run it.

vllm.explain: A fast model server for GPUs. It can run on another machine. Connect it to Mesbah by its address.

ollama.explain: A program that runs language models on a personal computer. Connect it to Mesbah by its address.

dataset.explain: A collection of examples a model learns from. Each example is one row, either a conversation or a piece of text.

subset.explain: Some datasets come in several variants, such as one for each language or task. Each variant is a subset.

split.explain: A part of a dataset kept for one use, such as train for training or test for checking the result.

jsonl.explain: A text file with one record on each line. Every dataset is saved this way, one row on each line.

rank.explain: The size of the LoRA add-on. A larger rank can learn more and needs more memory and disk space.

attention.explain: The part of each layer that links every token to the ones before it, to find what matters. Its modules are q_proj, k_proj, v_proj and o_proj.

feed_forward.explain: The part of each layer that processes every token on its own after attention. Most of a model's parameters sit here. Its modules are gate_proj, up_proj and down_proj.
